title: Build Your First PBL Project with Gemini Notebook and Make Student Portfolio Slides That Can Be Printed Offline
author: Phillip Alcock
summary: Phillip Alcock gives teachers a step-by-step workflow for planning a complete project-based learning unit inside one Gemini Notebook and generating a printable student portfolio slide deck from the same sources. The worked example has Years 5 to 8 investigate school water waste and build a measured fix. Teachers load approved sources, draft and revise a plan with a sources-only prompt that marks gaps, then paste a detailed design brief into the Slide Deck tool, fix slides with Revise, and download PowerPoint and PDF for printing. Each step has a check before moving on. The core argument is that the design brief is the reusable asset, and that teachers keep the factual and assessment decisions.
points: Load only teacher-approved unit sources and test that the chat cites them correctly before drafting anything.
The planning prompt restricts the AI to the notebook sources and requires gaps to be marked rather than invented.
A detailed design brief with a slide map, print-safe design rules and content rules controls the portfolio deck.
The worked project has students take before-and-after water measurements and justify a design with evidence.
After the first run, repair the design brief rather than just the deck, since the brief carries into next term.
quotes: This brief is the custom instruction set for the deck. It is long because everything you leave out gets decided by a default.
The AI built the empty portfolio structure. Every claim inside it is the student’s own measurement or a source the student can point to.
Look for a before and after measurement pair stated in numbers, and a design change the student can trace to feedback or to a result.
The prompt keeps subject facts inside your sources and asks for gaps to be flagged rather than filled.
After the first project, note which slide students filled in least and which instruction in the design brief you had to repair. Update the brief, not just the deck.
Open two or three sources after uploading and confirm the text loaded correctly, since a scanned PDF with unreadable text gives the chat nothing to work from.
